newsitem.title: MEXICO: Ford to up output by 25 pct at Mexico plant.
newsitem.headline: Ford to up output by 25 pct at Mexico plant.

text.p: U.S. car giant Ford Motor Co said on Wednesday it plans to increase its 1997 production by 25 percent at one of its key Mexican plants despite suspending production over the next two weeks.
The company plans to increase output at its Cuatitlan plant, in the state of Mexico, this year to 106,000 units from 85,000 in 1996, Ford said in a statement.
"Not withstanding the temporary suspension of production at the Contour/Mystique plant, Ford plans to increase vehicle production in Cuatitlan by 25 percent," it said.
The plant will stop producing its Contour and Mystique vehicles for two weeks to adjust its inventories to demand from the United States, which absorbs most of its production.
This year Ford plans to export 75,000 cars, 35 percent more than last year.
The company said that during the two-week suspension, workers would receive 75 percent of their salaries and 100 percent of their benefits.
"The stoppage involves 850 workers out of a total of 4,000 who are working in the Cuatitlan complex," Ford said. ((--Veronica Galan, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-9553))
